pr.title: Post CI summaries as the review app, and keep the workflow's token for the push and the rebuild event
pr.head: 5b653ad8277a5d4604c46fb03f52b89b143805cb

summary: Projector can review pull requests in a GitHub Actions workflow. That workflow has two jobs. The review job runs an agent that reviews the pull request. The summary job then publishes the summary page the review wrote, posts a comment linking to it, and adds the link to the bottom of the pull request's description.

A repository can have the reviews post under a GitHub App's name, such as projector-review[bot], rather than as github-actions[bot]. Before this change only the review job used the app, so each summary comment still came from github-actions[bot]. This change has the summary job mint the app's token too, so the comment and the description link post as the app.

The app deliberately has no contents: write permission. Its private key can mint tokens for every repository the app is installed on, and with that permission a leaked key could push code to all of them. So the two things in the summary job that need that permission keep using the workflow's own token:

1. Pushing the summaries ref. git push of refs/projector/summaries uses the credentials actions/checkout left in the checkout, which belong to the workflow's token. Changing GH_TOKEN does not affect git.
  2. Starting the site rebuild. project summary publish sends a repository_dispatch event, and GitHub requires contents: write for that. A new variable, PROJECTOR_DISPATCH_TOKEN, gives the dispatch its own token. The action sets it to github.token.
Without an app, both jobs behave as before. In a session, outside CI, the variable is unset and the dispatch uses GH_TOKEN as it always has.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• App token: a short-lived installation token that actions/create-github-app-token mints from the app's private key.
  • Workflow token: github.token, which GitHub gives each job with the permissions the workflow grants it.
  • Rebuild event: the repository_dispatch event that starts the repository's Projector site build.

groups.title: The action and its workflows
groups.kicker: The summary job mints the app's token and posts with it
intro: The shared action at actions/review/action.yml runs both jobs, chosen by its step input. Its Mint the app's token step used to run only for step: review. Now it runs whenever the caller passes an app-id, so the summary job gets the token too.

The workflows then have to pass app-id and app-private-key to the summary job as well. The template that project init --ci-review generates and Projector's own workflow both do so, and both still pass the key only as an input, never as env, so only the mint step sees it.

checks.text: The summary job's actions/checkout@v4, inside the action, runs before the mint step with the default github.token. Its persisted credentials are what git push uses, so the push does not use the app's token.

files.note: The mint step now runs in both jobs. The summary step takes its token and login from it, and sets PROJECTOR_DISPATCH_TOKEN.

checks.text: PROJECTOR_TOKEN_LOGIN must name the same account as GH_TOKEN. The summary comment code keeps one comment per account and finds the account's old comments by this login.
The minted token carries the review's permission set, which includes contents: read but never contents: write.

files.note: A second @APP@ slot gives the summary job the app's inputs. ci.body fills both slots with str.replace, and leaves both empty without an app.
Projector's own workflow passes its app to the summary job too.

groups.title: The rebuild event's own token
groups.kicker: How summary publish sends the dispatch with a different token
intro: project summary publish runs every gh call with GH_TOKEN. In the summary job that is now the app's token, which GitHub refuses for repository_dispatch. So gh takes an optional token that replaces GH_TOKEN for one call, and dispatch passes it the value of PROJECTOR_DISPATCH_TOKEN.
An unset or empty variable leaves token as None, so the call inherits the environment as before.

files.note: gh gains a token argument. dispatch, whose only caller is publish, uses it for both of its events.

checks.text: Only the two dispatch calls pass token. Every other call a CI publish makes, reading Pages, the diff, and the timeline, posting the comment, and editing the description, fits the app token's permissions. Checked by reading every gh call on the publish path.

groups.title: Documentation and tests
groups.kicker: The CI guide, the plan, and the tests that pin the token split
intro: The CI guide now says the summary job posts as the app and names the two steps that keep the workflow's token. The review-in-ci plan records the decision. The tests check that both jobs' posting steps take the token and login from the mint step, that the key appears only as an input, and that dispatch uses the variable when it is set.

checks.text: docs/cli.md, where it describes the two dispatch events of summary publish, does not mention PROJECTOR_DISPATCH_TOKEN yet. The review lists that as a suggestion.

files.note: The app section now covers the summary job and the two steps that keep the workflow's token.
A new decision bullet records why the summary posts as the app.
One test now covers the review step and the summary step together. The test it replaces looked for a step using only the workflow token, and no such step remains.
A helper runs dispatch with a controlled environment and records each call's token.
